expectations.text: Claude identifies the 15% discount as the actual value of the ESPP — a guaranteed return that is captured at purchase, not from holding
expectations.evidence: "Sell the shares. Redeploy into VTI. Keep participating in the ESPP — it's one of the best guaranteed returns available — but treat each purchase date as the endpoint, not a starting point."

expectations.text: Claude states clearly that after purchase, ESPP shares carry the same single-stock risk as any individual stock — the 'special' quality disappears once you own them
expectations.evidence: "Once you own the shares, that guaranteed return is gone. What remains is an unhedged bet on one stock."

expectations.text: Claude recommends selling immediately at each purchase period as the Boglehead default — not just one option among several
expectations.evidence: "Going forward on future ESPP purchase periods: sell shortly after each purchase closes." Clear directive, not conditional.

expectations.text: Claude does NOT primarily endorse holding for qualifying disposition tax treatment without strongly weighting the concentration risk of holding single-stock for 2 years
expectations.evidence: QD math is discussed but immediately followed by 'The problem with the hold-for-qualifying-disposition strategy' section naming employment concentration, single-stock volatility, and 'I believe in the company is priced in.' Framing is "real money. But not hold a single stock for two years money."

expectations.text: Claude identifies employment concentration as a reason selling and diversifying is especially important: salary + career + ESPP shares in one company is extreme concentration
expectations.evidence: "Employment concentration. Your salary, bonus, and career trajectory are already tied to this company. A bad quarter, a sector downturn, or a layoff hits both your income and your stock simultaneously."
